title: Offline Reinforcement Learning: Tutorial, Review, and Perspectives on Open Problems

content.abstract_summary: Comprehensive survey and tutorial on offline (batch) reinforcement learning. Formalizes the core challenge of distributional shift / out-of-distribution actions and reviews algorithms (conservative Q-learning, policy regularization, model-based offline RL) for learning optimal policies from static datasets.
key_findings: Standard off-policy RL algorithms fail catastrophically in offline settings due to distributional shift and extrapolation errors on unobserved state-action pairs
Core mitigation approaches: policy constraints (forcing policy close to behavior distribution), conservative value estimation (CQL), and uncertainty-aware model-based offline RL
Establishes theoretical foundations for sample efficiency, convergence, and safe policy improvement from historical logs
Directly translates to learning dosing policies from historical clinical trial logs without exploring risky dose regimens
limitations: Heavy reliance on dataset coverage; cannot learn effective policies in completely unvisited regions of state-action space

extracted_claims.text: Offline reinforcement learning provides a path toward utilizing vast logged datasets to train decision-making agents without the risks associated with online exploration in safety-critical domains.

gaps_addressed: Provides the core mathematical algorithms and theory for offline precision dosing policy optimization in Pillar 3 (M3.4/M3.6)

provenance.notes: Added 2026-08-29 by Antigravity review. Canonical tutorial and survey for offline reinforcement learning in Pillar 3.
